title: Request Classification and Observability Contracts for Runtime Routing
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This page defines the request classification model and the corresponding observability contract used across the serving runtime. The goal is to produce deterministic routing decisions, consistent SLO mapping, and standardized telemetry that enables rapid triage and automated policy enforcement (e.g., cost-aware routing, fallback decisions, and quality guards). This is an engineering-facing spec intended for runtime, router, and telemetry consumers.

Scope

- Applies to all inbound inference requests processed by Redwood public and dedicated runtimes.
- Covers: request tagging, workload classes, priority heuristics, routing attributes, required telemetry fields, and common debugging workflows.
- Excludes: IAM/auth schemes, billing pipeline (except for reference label mapping), and model content inspection for privacy.

Why this matters

Inconsistent request semantics produce noisy SLO attribution, incorrect capacity decisions, and inaccurate cost signals. Aligning on a single classification scheme reduces variance in routing outcomes and enables reusable dashboards, alert rules, and automated remediation.

Definitions

1) Workload class: A short label describing the expected performance and quality envelope for the request. Examples: "realtime", "interactive", "batch", "embedding-internal", "low_priority_scrape".
2) Priority: Discrete integer (0..9) used by schedulers to shape kernel allocation and preemption policies. 0 is highest priority (system-critical).
3) Route intent: High-level objective for the request (e.g., "low_latency", "low_cost", "high_quality").
4) Fingerprint: Stable hash of request properties used to group similar requests across telemetry and cache keying.

Contract: Required request attributes

Every request that enters a runtime path must include at minimum the following envelope attributes. If missing, the router will fill with conservative defaults and emit a visibility warning (see Debugging section).

- request_id: UUID v4
- client_id: team or org identifier
- model: model name or alias (string)
- model_version: semver-like or sha tag
- workload_class: one of (realtime, interactive, batch, embedding, maintenance)
- priority: integer 0..9
- route_intent: one of (low_latency, low_cost, high_quality, degrade_gracefully)
- sequence_hint: expected token count (optional but recommended for long-form workloads)
- fingerprint: hex encoded sha1 of canonicalized attributes (see fingerprinting rules)
- provenance: origin (api, console, sdk, internal)
- ttl_ms: optional time-to-live for queued work

Fingerprinting rules (stable, language-agnostic)

1) Canonicalization order: client_id, model, model_version, workload_class, route_intent, sequence_hint (empty values omitted).
2) Normalization: lowercase strings, trim whitespace, replace multiple spaces with single space.
3) Hashing: sha1(canonical_string) and hex-encode.
4) Example canonical string: "acme:bert:2026-01-02:interactive:low_latency:512" -> fingerprint: "e6f3..."

Workload class semantics and SLO mapping

- realtime: Target p95 latency <= 120ms; used for websockets, streaming endpoints. Priority default 3.
- interactive: Target p95 latency <= 350ms; used for chat-like UX. Priority default 4.
- batch: No strict latency SLO; throughput and cost are primary. Priority default 7.
- embedding: Target p95 latency <= 300ms for dedicated embedding endpoints. Priority default 5.
- maintenance: For scheduled background tasks; can be preempted aggressively. Priority default 9.

Routing policy precedence (ordered)

1) Explicit route bindings (customer-specified pin)
2) SLO-driven routing (map workload_class -> compatible model variants)
3) Cost policy (if route_intent == low_cost)
4) Capacity availability fallback (regional/variant fallthrough)
5) Canary/rollout overrides (if in canary window and route matches)

Telemetry contract (required fields for ingestion)

Telemetry must be emitted at three points: router-in (accept), runtime-start, runtime-complete. Each emission is a JSON line with the following flat keys. All keys are strings unless noted. Timestamp fields are ISO8601 UTC.

Required fields (all events):
- ts_iso: timestamp
- event_type: router-in | runtime-start | runtime-complete
- request_id
- fingerprint
- client_id
- model
- model_version
- workload_class
- priority (stringified int)
- route_intent
- selected_variant (the variant/kind chosen or "none")
- region
- node_id (when available)
- seq_len_hint (if present)

Additional fields (runtime-complete):
- latency_ms (integer)
- tokens_out (integer)
- tokens_in (integer)
- error_code (empty if success)
- preempted (true|false)
- cost_estimate_usd (string)

Example telemetry lines:

router-in:
{
  "ts_iso": "2026-02-12T20:34:12.123Z",
  "event_type": "router-in",
  "request_id": "4a1f...",
  "fingerprint": "e6f3...",
  "client_id": "acme",
  "model": "gpt-redwood-3b",
  "model_version": "v2026-02-01",
  "workload_class": "interactive",
  "priority": "4",
  "route_intent": "low_latency",
  "selected_variant": "gpu-v1",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "node_id": "node-42"
}

runtime-complete:
{
  "ts_iso": "2026-02-12T20:34:12.501Z",
  "event_type": "runtime-complete",
  "request_id": "4a1f...",
  "fingerprint": "e6f3...",
  "latency_ms": 378,
  "tokens_out": 120,
  "tokens_in": 24,
  "error_code": "",
  "preempted": "false",
  "cost_estimate_usd": "0.0032"
}

Derived metrics and dashboards (minimum set)

- p50/p95/p99 latency per workload_class x model_variant
- success_rate (1 - error_rate) per priority bucket
- preemption_rate per client_id and workload_class
- cost_per_1k_tokens by model_variant and region
- queue_depth and wait_time distributions for batch queues

Alerting guidelines

- Latency SLO breach: if p95(realtime) > 120ms for 10m with volume > 10 req/s -> P1 page and trigger fallback routing to low-latency variants.
- Unexpected preemption spike: preemption_rate increase by 5x relative to 1h baseline -> P2 investigate kernel fairness and priority inversion.
- Fingerprint drift: sudden >40% increase in unique fingerprints for a client in 30m -> P2 check client SDK changes or bot traffic.

Debugging checklist (fast path)

1) Confirm router-in event exists for request_id. If absent, check ingress hooks and SDK instrumentation.
2) Validate fingerprint consistency across router-in and runtime-complete. Mismatches indicate canonicalization bugs.
3) If high latency, query node_id and run quick diagnostics: gpu utilization, kernel queue length, eviction_count.
4) For preemptions, inspect kernel-scheduler logs and priority queues for inversion traces.
5) If cost unexpectedly high, check selected_variant and route_intent; ensure quantized variant was eligible.

Common misconfigurations and remediations

- Missing sequence_hint: For long-form interactive tasks, omission causes kernel to select conservative unbatched path. Remediation: Upgrade SDK to v1.8+ or set default seq_len_hint on the route.
- Incorrect workload_class mapping from SDK: Use migration script provided in tools/routing-migrate.sh.
- Fingerprinting version skew: Ensure all SDKs use fingerprint spec v2.0 (see appendix) or enable compatibility header "Fingerprint-Version: v1".

Operational playbook: automated remediation examples

1) Auto-fallback on SLO breach:
   - Trigger: p95(realtime) > 120ms for 10m
   - Action: Router attaches tag "fallback_low_latency" and re-routes new requests to cached low-latency variants for 5m.
   - Postmortem: Create alert ticket and run throughput simulation against captured traces.

2) Auto-throttle noisy client:
   - Trigger: unique_fingerprints_per_minute(client_id) > threshold AND error_rate > 1%
   - Action: Inject rate-limit header, shadow route to cost-tiered variant, notify account owner.

Appendix A: Configuration examples

YAML: route binding example

routes:
  - name: acme-realtime
    client_id: acme
    workload_class: realtime
    default_priority: 3
    allowed_variants: ["gpu-v1", "gpu-small-v2"]
    route_intent: low_latency
    fallback_order: ["gpu-small-v2", "cpu-quantized"]

CLI snippet: emit a router-in test event

$ ./tools/emit-test-telemetry --type router-in --request-id 0000-1111 --client acme --model gpt-redwood-3b --workload interactive

Appendix B: Fingerprint compatibility table

| SDK version | fingerprint spec | notes |
|-------------|------------------|-------|
| 1.x         | v1               | legacy: canonicalization omitted sequence_hint |
| 2.0         | v2               | current: canonicalization includes sequence_hint and route_intent |
| 2.1+        | v2               | adds optional deterministic client-salt header |

Ownership and rollout plan

- Owner: runtime-routing team (primary), telemetry-shared (secondary)
- Rollout: SDK + router integration to be staged across canary -> region-wide over 6 weeks.
- Migration windows: SDKs older than 2.0 will be supported with compatibility headers for 90 days.

Open items and future work

- Formalize a bounded vocabulary for route_intent to support programmatic policy synthesis.
- Investigate compact binary telemetry envelope for high-throughput short events.
